A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same XQC research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching the theoretical appendix moved from I in v1 to J in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original XQC experiments on 55 proprioceptive and 15 vision-based control tasks, Hessian analyses, and architectural ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds measured computational throughput, additional architectural controls, and conditioning results.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same SAC-based XQC architecture, batch normalization, weight projection, categorical cross-entropy critic, reward normalization, and vision encoder. Skip connections and other new configurations are investigated as ablations without changing the proposed default method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 55 proprioceptive tasks across HumanoidBench, DMC, MyoSuite, and MuJoCo, plus 15 vision-based DMC tasks. The added timing and conditioning experiments use existing humanoid and dog-trot environments.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain their baseline sets, including SIMBA-V2, BRO, MRQ, BRC, CROSSQ+WN, SAC, and DRQ-V2. The new timing comparison uses existing baselines; additional XQC variants serve as ablations.

E3.justification: Table 2 changes the reported vision replay-buffer capacity from 10M to 1M for both XQC and DRQ-V2, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Added protocols include training/evaluation FPS measurements on MuJoCo humanoid and controlled variations of batch size, action repetition, weight decay, skip connections, and learning rate.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's component-removal and scaling studies, v2 tests skip connections, batch sizes 128/512, weight decay, action repetition, and a halved learning rate for the LN variant. New Appendix I examines conditioning under architectural and optimization variations, substantially broadening sensitivity tests and checks of the proposed mechanism.

E5.justification: Appendices D–E add arithmetic-mean curves with 90% SBCIs alongside the existing IQM summaries. This expands statistical estimation and reporting, while the stated seed counts and confidence level remain unchanged; additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: v2 adds throughput measurements, extended ablation/conditioning results, and mean-return curves across all 70 tasks. Existing IQM curves also change: Figure 6 revises XQC's MyoSuite score from 0.85 to 0.84 and MuJoCo score from 1.13 to 1.16, retaining the overall 0.73. New Figure 10 reports 0.29 for the halved-rate LN variant versus 0.44 at the original rate.

T1.justification: The definitions, Assumption 1, Theorem 1, propositions, and proofs are retained. The theoretical appendix moves from I to J; the new conditioning experiments introduce no new formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims that BN, WN, and categorical cross-entropy improve critic conditioning and enable strong sample efficiency across the same 70 tasks with fewer parameters. Additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly explains slightly slower inference than SIMBA-V2 through larger policy networks and contextualizes throughput against typical control frequencies. Section 5.4 interprets the unsuccessful lower-learning-rate LN control as supporting the conditioning explanation. The conclusion adds prospective model-based, imitation-learning, and prior-dataset applications.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project/code-access URL in the abstract, RTX 4090 hardware information for timing, and settings for new controls, including weight decay of 1e-4. Table 2 revises replay capacity. The reproducibility statement nevertheless retains v1's promise to release code upon acceptance.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on robotics, learning with offline data, model-based and imitation learning, and target-network design. Section 6 positions Vincent et al. (2026) and Hendawy et al. (2026) as orthogonal approaches, while preserving the paper's central optimization-based positioning.

P1.justification: There are localized introduction rewrites, terminology and typo edits, expanded experimental discussion and future work, and updated publication headers. The main section organization remains stable; inserting Appendix I renumbers the proof appendix to J.

P2.justification: Figures are extensively recolored and reformatted, including marker, legend, and axis changes. Former Figure 9 is reorganized into efficiency Figure 9 and scaling/ablation Figure 10. New throughput panels, five mean-curve figures, and conditioning Figure 25 substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Measured training and inference throughput in Section 5.3 and the additional controls in Section 5.4 and Appendix I strengthen support for existing efficiency and conditioning arguments. Mean-return summaries and code-access information also aid assessment and reproducibility. These gains are modest overall, with unexplained revisions to some retained curves and the replay-buffer setting leaving reporting ambiguities.
